rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous who seek the Hereafter do its proper work while affirming God's oneness; God thanks their effort by rewarding them with Paradise.
rows.anchor: من الأبرار بعمله الحسن، وهو مؤمن، يعني بالدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Bilal the muezzin and others.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بلال المؤذن وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies both righteous Muslims and the disbelieving people of Thaqif; His provision is not withheld from either group.
rows.anchor: عطآء ربك } ، يعني رزق ربك، { وما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelieving Thaqif had more worldly provision than Bilal and his righteous companions, but the believers receive far greater favor in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: أعطى هؤلاء المؤمنون بلال ومن معه، أعطوا في الآخرة فضلا كبيرا أكثر مما أعطى الفجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to associate another god is addressed to Muhammad when he was invited to his forefathers' religion; the associator ends blamed by people and forsaken in God's punishment.
rows.anchor: فتقعد مذموما } ، ملوما تلام عند الناس، { مخذولا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reportedly had a codex reading wa-waṣṣā rabbuka; Muqatil explains the received wa-qaḍā as meaning that God charged or commanded.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، أنه كان في المصحف: ووصى ربك، فالتزق الواو بالصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command is that people worship and affirm none but Him, and treat their parents with dutiful kindness.
rows.anchor: قضى ربك } ، يعني وعهد ربك، { ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil associates the parents in this instruction with Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
rows.anchor: يعني أبويه، يعني سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children must not utter degrading words, including wishing their parents' death, or speak harshly while caring for them in old age or cleaning them.
rows.anchor: اللهم أرحنى منهما، أو تغلظ عليهما في القول عند كبرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke parents during their care; speak to them with gracious, gentle words.
rows.anchor: ولا تنهرهما } عند المعالجة، يعني تغلظ لهما القول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children should show their parents humble tenderness out of compassion and ask God to have mercy on them as they cared for the child.
rows.anchor: تلين جناحك لهما رحمة بهما { وقل رب ارحمهما } عندما تعالج منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be gentle with parents but disobey them in polytheism; disobedience on that point does not sever kinship.
rows.anchor: فالطف بهما، واعصهما في الشرك، فإنه ليس معصيتك إياهما في الشرك قطيعة لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for the parents' mercy was abrogated by the prohibition on believers seeking forgiveness for polytheist relatives.
rows.anchor: ثم نسخت: { كما ربياني صغيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether people inwardly intend good toward elderly parents and whether they count the effort of caring for them; He forgives those who turn from sins to obey their parents.
rows.anchor: يقول: هو أعلم بما في نفوسكم منكم من البر للوالدين عند كبرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give relatives their due by maintaining ties, give charity to the person who asks, and show kindness to a guest traveling away from home.
rows.anchor: يعني فأعط، { ذا القربى حقه } ، يعني صلته، ثم قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasteful spenders are those who spend outside what is right.
rows.anchor: يعني المنفقين في غير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who spend wrongly, identified here as Meccan unbelievers, are Satan's brothers through their disobedience; Satan means Iblis, disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: يعني المنفقين، يعني كفار مكة، في غير حق، { كانوا إخوان الشياطين } في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns poor people including Khabbab, Bilal, Mihja, and Ammar who asked Muhammad for help when he had nothing to give and turned away silently.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خباب، وبلال، ومهجع، وعمار، ونحوهم من الفقراء، كانوا يسألون النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unable to give, Muhammad should offer the poor a kind reply and a hopeful promise of future provision.
rows.anchor: يعني انتظار رزق من ربك، { فقل لهم قولا ميسورا } [آية: 28]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses burying daughters alive from fear of poverty; God provides for parents and children, and killing them is a grave sin.
rows.anchor: يعني دفن البنات وهن أحياء، { خشية إملاق } ، يعني مخافة للفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zina is disobedience and an evil path; at that time it had no prescribed penalty, which came later in the Medinan surah al-Nur.
rows.anchor: يعني معصية، { وسآء سبيلا } [آية: 32]، يعني المسلك، لم يكن يومئذ في الزنا حد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An heir to a person killed unjustly may choose retaliation, pardon, or blood money; the execution must be limited to the killer, since killing another person is excess.
rows.anchor: يعني مسلطا على القتلى إن شاء قبله، وإن شاء عفا عنه، وإن شاء أخذ الدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heir's authority is established by God's command in Scripture, and the unjustly killed person is supported by God.
rows.anchor: من أمر الله عز وجل في كتابه، جعل الأمر إليه، ولا تقتلن غير القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use an orphan's property only in a way that grows it through profit; Muqatil says this rule was abrogated by the allowance to associate with orphans as brothers.
rows.anchor: إلا لتنمي ماله بالأرباح، نسختها: وإن تخالطوهم فإخوانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan reaches full maturity at eighteen years.
rows.anchor: يعني ثماني عشرة سنة، { وأوفوا بالعهد } فيما بينكم وبين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keep covenants made with other people, since God will question people about broken covenants in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: إذا نقض، { كان مسؤولا } [آية: 34]، يقول: الله سائلكم عنه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qistas means a balance in the Roman language; giving full measure and weight is better than shortchanging and has a better outcome in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني بالميزان بلغة الروم، { المستقيم ذلك } الوفاء، { خير } من النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not accuse others of polytheism without knowledge that God has a partner; hearing, sight, and heart will be questioned about shirk in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولا ترم بالشرك، فإنه ليس لك به علم أن لي شريكا، ثم حذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking arrogantly expresses grandeur, conceit, and pride; the arrogant cannot pierce the earth or reach the mountains in height.
rows.anchor: يعني بالعظمة، والخيلاء، والكبرياء، { إنك لن تخرق الأرض } إذا مشيت بالخيلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands and prohibitions in these verses are in view: neglecting commands and doing what God prohibited is disliked by Him.
rows.anchor: يعني ترك ما أمر الله عز وجل به، ونهى عنه في هؤلاء الآيات، أي وركوب ما نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding commands and prohibitions are wisdom revealed to Muhammad; associating another god would leave the person self-blaming and banished in Hell.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك الذي أمر الله به ونهى عنه في هؤلاء الآيات، { من الحكمة } التي أوحاها إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madḥūr means driven away, as in the verse about being pelted from every side.
rows.anchor: يعني مطرودا في النار، كقوله سبحانه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes Meccan polytheists for claiming that God chose sons for them but took daughters, meaning female angels, for Himself.
rows.anchor: قل يا محمد لكفار مكة: { أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين } ، نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that angels are God's daughters is an outrageous statement; this verse followed the reference to their claim about other gods.
rows.anchor: حين قالوا: الملائكة بنات الرحمن، { واتخذ } لنفسه { من الملائكة إناثا } ، يعني البنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an varies its subjects so people will learn, yet it only increases the unbelievers' distance from belief.
rows.anchor: في أمور شتى، { ليذكروا } فيعتبروا، { وما يزيدهم } القرآن، { إلا نفورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel phrase in al-Mulk uses نفور to mean distance or turning away.
rows.anchor: بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists worship angels, whom they claim are daughters of the Merciful, hoping they will intercede; if there were other gods, they would contend with the Lord of the Throne as earthly kings do.
rows.anchor: حين يزعمون أن الملائكة بنات الرحمن، فيعبدونهم ليشفعوا لهم عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted far above the false claims made about Him.
rows.anchor: نزه نفسه تعالى عن قول البهتان، فقال: { وتعالى } ، يعني وارتفع، { عما يقولون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All seven heavens, earth, and everything in them remember and glorify God by His command, including plants, animals, and other created things; people do not hear their praise.
rows.anchor: يعني تذكره، { السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء } ، يعني وما من شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunder's glorification is likewise by God's command, as is the praise of plants and creatures.
rows.anchor: يعني بأمره، من نبت، أو دابة، أو خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing and forgiving toward the polytheists: He overlooks their claims that He has partners and delays their punishment until its appointed time.
rows.anchor: حين لا يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة، { غفورا } في تأخير العذاب عنهم إلى المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's preservation of the heavens and earth from vanishing is another parallel concerning His forbearance.
rows.anchor: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier is set when Muhammad recites during prayer or outside it; the unbelievers do not affirm resurrection and its recompense.
rows.anchor: في الصلاة أو غير الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden barrier verse was revealed concerning Abu Lahab and his wife, Abu al-Bukhturi, Zamʿah (whose name was ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad), Suhayl, and Huwaytib, all Quraysh.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي لهب وامرأته، وأبي البحتري، وزمعة اسمه عمرو بن الأسود، وسهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God puts coverings on hearts to prevent understanding the Qur'an and heaviness in ears to prevent hearing it.
rows.anchor: يعني الغطاء على القلوب، { أن يفقهوه } ، لئلا يفقهوا القرآن، { وفي آذانهم وقرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God alone means saying there is no god but God; opponents turn away in aversion to monotheism.
rows.anchor: فقلت: لا إله إلا الله، { ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا } [آية: 46]، يعني أعرضوا عن التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Meccan leaders visited Abu Talib, Muhammad asked them to say the declaration of God's oneness, promising that Arabs would submit and non-Arabs would obey them.
rows.anchor: قولوا: لا إله إلا الله، تملكون بها العرب وتدين لكم العجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders secretly discussed Muhammad's recitation; the parallel in al-Anbiya quotes them asking whether he is merely a human and whether they knowingly approach magic.
rows.anchor: وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressors are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and his companions, who claimed followers followed only a bewitched man; bewitched means overcome in reason.
rows.anchor: يعني الوليد بن المغيرة وأصحابه، { إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same accusation appears in al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called Muhammad a sorcerer and thereby strayed from guidance, with no way out of their false accusation.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يقدرون على مخرج مما قالوا لك بأنك ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rufat means dust; the unbelievers ask whether they will be raised anew after death.
rows.anchor: يعني ترابا، { أإنا لمبعوثون } بعد الموت، { خلقا جديدا } [آية: 49]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if people became stone, iron, or another form they regard as mighty, God can raise them; the One who first created them will restore them.
rows.anchor: يعني مما يعظم في قلوبكم، قل لو كنتم أنتم الموت لأمتكم ثم بعثتكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shake their heads in mockery and denial when asking when resurrection will happen; Muhammad is told to say it may be soon.
rows.anchor: يعني يهزون إليك، { رؤوسهم } استهزاء وتكذيبا بالبعث، { ويقولون متى هو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the day God calls people from their graves, they answer His caller by His command and think their stay was brief.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن إسرافيل قائم على صخرة بيت المقدس يدعو أهل القبور في قرن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israfil will stand on a rock in Jerusalem and call the scattered flesh, veins, and hair to emerge for judgment, receive their souls, and be recompensed for their deeds.
rows.anchor: فيقول: أيتها اللحوم المتفرقة وأيتها العروق المتقطعة، وأيتها الشعور المتفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who emerge from their graves hurry toward the caller, as described in Yasin.
rows.anchor: ويديم المنادي الصوت، فيخرجون من قبورهم، ويسمعون الصوت، فيسعون إليه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: The command to speak in the best way addressed Umar after a Meccan unbeliever insulted him and Umar nearly retaliated; God ordered pardon and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يعني عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، { يقولوا التي هي أحسن } ، ليرد خيرا على من شتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same command to believers appears in al-Jathiya.
rows.anchor: نظيرها في الجاثية: قل للذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan incites hostility among people and is plainly their enemy.
rows.anchor: يعني يغري بينهم، { إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy by granting repentance or punish by causing people to die in disbelief; Muhammad is not their controller.
rows.anchor: فيتوب عليكم، { أو إن يشأ يعذبكم } ، فيميتكم على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in al-Ahzab says God will punish hypocritical men and women.
rows.anchor: نظيرها في الأحزاب، ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ranked the prophets through distinct gifts: speaking with God, friendship with Him, command of birds and mountains, great sovereignty, raising the dead and healing, or being raised to heaven.
rows.anchor: منهم من كلم الله، ومنهم من اتخذه الله خليلا، ومنهم من سخر الله له الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David was given a Psalter of 150 chapters containing praise and glorification but no legal rulings, obligations, permissions, or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: مائة وخمسين سورة، ليس فيها حكم، ولا حد، ولا فريضة، ولا حلال، ولا حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings Meccans call on besides God are angels; they cannot relieve or transfer the seven-year famine that struck Mecca, during which people ate carrion, dogs, and carcasses.
rows.anchor: من دون الله يعني الملائكة، فليكشفوا الضر عنكم، يعني الجوع سبع سنين إذا نزل بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel in Saba says the supposed gods do not own even a tiny ant; Muqatil describes it as a tiny red ant barely visible.
rows.anchor: يعني أصغر النمل التي لا تكاد أن ترى من الصغر، وهى النملة الحمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels themselves seek closeness to God through obedience, each hoping for the nearest rank; wasila means nearness, as in al-Maida.
rows.anchor: يعني الزلفة، وهي القربة بطاعتهم، { أيهم أقرب } إلى الله درجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels hope for God's mercy, meaning Paradise, and fear His punishment; people should seek nearness, hope, and fear as they do.
rows.anchor: يعني الملائكة، { إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا } [آية: 57]، يقول: يحذره الخائفون له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town, righteous or wicked, is destined for destruction or severe punishment before the Resurrection: the righteous die, while the wicked are punished in this world.
rows.anchor: فأما الصالحة، فهلاكها بالموت، وأما الطالحة، فيأخذها العذاب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fate is written in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: يعني في أم الكتاب مكتوبا، يعني اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and al-Harith ibn Hisham of the Makhzum clan asked Muhammad to show signs as earlier peoples had seen.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي أمية بن المغيرة، والحارث بن هشام بن المغيرة المخزوميين، سألا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because earlier peoples rejected signs and were destroyed, the requested signs were withheld lest the Meccans reject one and be destroyed likewise; signs are warnings, and Thamud denied and hamstrung the visible she-camel.
rows.anchor: يعني الأمم الخالية، فعذبتهم، ولو جئتهم بآية فردوها وكذبوا بها أهلكناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel was clearly visible, but Thamud denied that it came from God and hamstrung it; signs are sent to warn people of worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني معاينة يبصرونها، { فظلموا بها } ، يعني فجحدوا بها أنها ليست من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree in the Qur'an is Zaqqum, and the mockery that it was dates and butter contradicts the description of its fruit as resembling devils' heads.
rows.anchor: لقولهم الزقوم التمر والزبد: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl taunted Quraysh with dates as the promised Zaqqum, following ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubʿari's claim that the word meant dates and butter in Berber.
rows.anchor: فقال لقريش وهم حوله: تزقموا من هذا الزقوم الذي يخوفكم به محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's encompassing of the people means His knowledge that He would give Muhammad victory over Mecca.
rows.anchor: أهل مكة أن يفتحها على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision was the Night Journey to Jerusalem, which became a trial for Meccans.
rows.anchor: ليلة أسري به إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accursed tree is Zaqqum; warnings about Fire and Zaqqum only increased the Meccans' severe transgression.
rows.anchor: يعني شجرة الزقوم، ثم قال سبحانه: { ونخوفهم } بها، يعني بالنار والزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl mocked the warning that a tree grows in Hell, while ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubʿari said zaqqum meant dates and butter in Berber; Abu Jahl then brought dates for Quraysh to mockingly eat.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: يا معشر قريش، إن محمدا يخوفكم بشجرة الزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl called dates Zaqqum to mock the warning, after ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubʿari's gloss.
rows.anchor: فقال لقريش وهم حوله: تزقموا من هذا الزقوم الذي يخوفكم به محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was among those commanded to bow to Adam but refused arrogantly, arguing that he was made from fire while Adam was made from clay.
rows.anchor: منهم إبليس، { فسجدوا } ثم استثنى، فقال: { إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis regarded Adam's commanded prostration as preference over himself and sought respite until Resurrection so he could seize Adam's descendants, except the few God willed.
rows.anchor: يعني فضلته علي بالسجود، يعني آدم، أنا ناري وهو طيني، { لئن أخرتن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's assurance that His servants are beyond Satan's authority means Satan has no dominion over them.
rows.anchor: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those among Adam's descendants who follow Satan's religion receive Hell as the ample recompense for their evil deeds and disbelief, with no relief from its torment.
rows.anchor: يعني وافرا لا يفتر عنهم من عذابها شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's voice is his call to lure people, and his horsemen are riders who travel in disobedience.
rows.anchor: يعني كل راكب يسير في معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's foot soldiers are any obedient jinn or human who walks in disobedience; he shares in illicit money and forbidden crops and livestock by making them attractive.
rows.anchor: كل راجل يمشي في معصية الله عز وجل من الجن والإنس من يطيعك منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies zina and every child conceived unlawfully among Satan's share and obedience.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: إن الزنا، والغضب، والأولاد، يعني كل ولد من حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan promises people delusion, including denying resurrection; such a promise is false and worthless.
rows.anchor: يعني ومنيهم الغرور ألا بعث، { وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sincere servants are beyond Satan's dominion to lead them into disbelief or shirk and away from guidance; God protects them so Iblis cannot reach them.
rows.anchor: ملك في الكفر والشرك أن تضلهم عن الهدى، { وكفى بربك وكيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gently drives ships through the sea so people can seek provision; this reflects His mercy.
rows.anchor: يعني يسوق لكم، { الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله } الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In distress at sea, false gods become ineffectual and people call only on God; after rescue to land they turn away from praying in ease and are ungrateful for not worshiping Him.
rows.anchor: فلا تدعونهم إنما تدعون الله عز وجل، فذلك قوله سبحانه: { إلا إياه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for false gods becoming lost or absent means their deeds are nullified, as in the parallel in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني بطل، مثل قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rescue, people should not feel safe from God sinking a part of the land or pelting them with stones; no protector can shield them from Him.
rows.anchor: يعني ناحية من البر، { أو يرسل عليكم } في البر { حاصبا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may return them to sea and send a violent wind to capsize them; this would be for ingratitude after rescue and breaking their covenant, with no one to exact retribution from God.
rows.anchor: فيغرقكم بما كفرتم } النعم حين أنجاكم من الغرق، ونقضتم العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabeʿa means an adverse consequence or liability for the punishment inflicted; they would find no one to pursue such a claim against God.
rows.anchor: لا تجدوا علينا به تبعة مما أصبناكم به من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is honored above other animals, though not angels, by eating and drinking with hands while animals and birds use their mouths.
rows.anchor: فضلناهم على غيرهم من الحيوان غير الملائكة حين أكلوا وشربوا بأيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People travel on mounts over land and ships at sea and receive good provisions beyond those of animals; the stated distinction is eating with hands.
rows.anchor: على الرطب، يعني الدواب، { و } حملناهم في { والبحر } ، على اليابس، يعني السفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community is summoned with its imam, meaning the book recording the good and evil it did in worldly life; the parallel in Yasin calls the Preserved Tablet a clear imam.
rows.anchor: يعني كل أمة بكتابهم الذى عملوا في الدنيا من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given their book in the right hand read the deeds they performed in life and are not wronged even by a date-stone's thread-like husk.
rows.anchor: الذي عملوه في الدنيا، { ولا يظلمون فتيلا } [آية: 71]، يعني بالفتيل القشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind person here is an unbeliever who sees worldly blessings but fails to recognize they come from God and so does not thank or affirm His oneness; in the Hereafter he is blind to resurrection, judgment, Paradise, and Hell and further astray.
rows.anchor: البعث والحساب والجنة والنار أعمى، { وأضل سبيلا } [آية: 72]، يعني وأخطأ طريقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who nearly diverted Muhammad from revelation were Thaqif; the warning parallels the command in al-Maida not to let people turn him from what was revealed.
rows.anchor: يعني ثقيفا، يقول: وقد كادوا أن يفتنوك، يعني قد هموا أن يصدوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqif approached Muhammad as brothers, in-laws, and neighbors, claiming that their submission or opposition would determine Najd's response, and demanded exemptions from prayer, almsgiving, smashing idols, debt obligations, protection of Wajj, and local appointments, plus one year for al-Lat.
rows.anchor: نحن إخوانك، وأصهارك، وجيرانك، ونحن خير أهل نجد لك سلما، وأضره عليك حربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad refused to exempt them from prayer and prostration, saying a religion without bowing and prostration is no good, but said others could be ordered to break their idols; he hesitated to reject the request to keep al-Lat for a year lest they refuse Islam.
rows.anchor: لا خير في دين ليس فيه ركوع ولا سجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar protested that Thaqif had hurt the Prophet by mentioning al-Lat, declaring God would not leave shirk in a land where He is worshiped and that they must either submit or leave.
rows.anchor: أحرقتم قلب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بذكر اللات، أحرق الله أكبادكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqif urged Muhammad to claim God had ordered him to leave al-Lat in their land; the verse warns against fabricating such a concession, which would have made them love him as a friend.
rows.anchor: فقل لهم: إن ربي أمرني أن أقر اللات بأرضهم سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical friendship means Thaqif would love Muhammad if he complied with their demands.
rows.anchor: لطواعيتكم إياهم على ما أرادوك عليه إذا لأحبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened Muhammad by his silence so he would order the idols destroyed; without that support he would have inclined briefly and slightly toward the requested disobedience.
rows.anchor: يا محمد بالسكوت، فأمرت بكسر الآلهة، إذا لركنت إلى المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukn means to incline, and the slight inclination is glossed by a brief moment; the parallel phrase in al-Dhariyat uses rukn for turning or leaning.
rows.anchor: يقول: لقد هممت سويعة أن تميل، { إليهم شيئا قليلا } [آية: 74]، يعني أمرا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Muhammad obeyed them, God would have made him taste doubled punishment in worldly life and after death, and he would have no protector against God.
rows.anchor: يقول سبحانه: إذا لأذقناك ضعف العذاب في الدنيا في حياتك، وفى مماتك بعد
